 About iPhone charge speeds
 Learn how to improve the charging speed of your iPhone.
 Get a charge-time estimate
 With iOS 26, to get an estimate of the time needed to charge your iPhone, open Settings and tap Battery. iOS estimates the time that it will take to charge to 80 percent, or to 100 percent (or your charge limit) if the charge level is over 80 percent. You can also see this estimate near the top of the Lock Screen.
 Charge faster with a different charger
 For faster wired charging, use a USB-C Power Delivery charger and a USB-C cable for iPhone 15 models and later 1 (or a USB-C to Lightning cable for iPhone 14 models and earlier).
 For faster wireless charging, use a MagSafe Charger 2 or a Qi2-certified wireless charger .
 Charging your iPhone might take longer than you expect if you use:
 A wired charger that provides 7.5W or less 
 A wireless charger that provides less than 10W, like a Qi1-certified charger
 If your wired charger has more than one port, like the 35W Dual USB-C Port Power Adapter, or if you charge with a computer or USB hub with other connected devices, the maximum power output might be reduced. This depends on the combined power needs of all connected devices and on system conditions. 
 Charge ports in USB hubs or cars might charge slower than a dedicated USB-C charger.
 Find out if you should use a different charger
 With iOS 18 and later, if a higher-wattage charger could improve your charging experience, iOS will display a Slow Charger message on the Lock Screen. You will also see this message when you open Settings and tap Battery. This doesn’t mean that there’s anything wrong with your iPhone or charger. You can tap the Info button to get more information.
 With iOS 26, if iOS detects a charger that's connected but isn't charging, you'll see an Incompatible Charger message when you open Settings and tap Battery.
 Charge faster
 Here are a few more ways to speed up charging. 
 Disconnect other accessories
 To comply with regulatory standards, if you connect USB-C or Lightning accessories (like headphones) while wirelessly charging your iPhone, the system limits charging to 7.5W.
 If an accessory with power pass-through (like a USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter) needs to reserve power for the ports, it might reduce the power delivered to your iPhone.
 For faster wireless charging, disconnect wired accessories from your iPhone.
 Limit your use of apps
 You might notice reduced charging speed if:
 You use graphics-intensive or processor-intensive apps, games, or features, including camera apps
 You stream high-quality video, especially with the display at full brightness
 If you need your iPhone to charge fast, limit your use of these apps while charging.
 Charge in a cooler place
 Your iPhone might get slightly warmer while it charges. Your iPhone might put charging on hold temporarily while in extreme temperature conditions . Charging will resume when the battery’s temperature returns to its normal operating range. Try moving your iPhone and charger to a cooler place.
 You can see if charging was on hold on your iPhone by opening Settings and tapping Battery.

 Fast charge your iPhone 
 With a USB-A charger, iPhone 15 models and later will charge at a maximum of 7.5W .
 MagSafe Battery Pack will show a Slow Charger message.

 Understand Thermally Limited Charging on iPhone
 Your iPhone protects its battery by limiting charging in hot or cold conditions.
 Charging your iPhone in very hot or cold environments can temporarily affect performance. When your iPhone becomes too warm or too cold, iOS may automatically slow down or pause charging. This helps preserve your battery’s long-term health and ensures safe operation.
 You might see a message on the Lock Screen such as “Charging On Hold. Charging will resume when iPhone returns to normal temperature.”
 What to expect
 If your iPhone gets too warm, charging may slow or stop until the temperature lowers.
 In very cold environments, charging may be slower or temporarily disabled until your device warms up.
 Charging resumes automatically when the battery returns to a safe temperature range.
 These protections apply whether you’re using a cable, MagSafe Charger, or other wireless chargers.
 Tips to maintain charging performance in extreme temperatures
 Help your iPhone charge efficiently with these best practices:
 Charge your iPhone in environments between 32° and 95° F (0° and 35° C).
 Avoid placing your iPhone in direct sunlight or leaving it in hot spaces (like a car on a sunny day).
 If you’re in a cold climate, try charging indoors or warming your iPhone gradually before plugging it in.
 Remove your case if your iPhone tends to heat up while charging.
 Note: These temperature-based protections work automatically and can’t be turned off. They are available on iPhone using iOS 16 or later.

 How to wirelessly charge your iPhone
 Learn how to wirelessly charge your iPhone with Qi-certified charging accessories.
 What you need
 You need an iPhone 8 or later .
 Your iPhone features integrated wireless charging that allows for an easy and intuitive charging experience. Your iPhone works with Qi-certified chargers that are available as accessories and in cars, cafes, hotels, airports, and furniture. Qi is an open, universal charging standard created by the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). 
 Many Qi-certified chargers charge iPhone with the latest version of iOS at rates up to 7.5 watts. These chargers are available at the Apple Online Store and Apple Stores.
 View a list of Qi-certified chargers . 
 Other Qi-certified chargers might vary in functionality and performance. If you have questions, contact the manufacturer.
 Charge wirelessly
 Connect your charger to power. Use the power adapter that came with your accessory or a power adapter recommended by the manufacturer.
 Place the charger on a level surface or other location recommended by the manufacturer.
 Place your iPhone on the charger with the display facing up. For best performance, place it in the center of the charger or in the location recommended by manufacturer.
 Your iPhone should start charging a few seconds after you place it on your wireless charger.
 You should see the Charging icon in the status bar.
 Learn more
 Wireless charging uses magnetic induction to charge your iPhone. Don't place anything between your iPhone and the charger. Magnetic mounts, magnetic cases, or other objects between your iPhone and the charger might reduce performance or damage magnetic strips or RFID chips like those found in some credit cards, security badges, passports, and key fobs. If your case holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging or make sure that they aren’t between the back of your iPhone and the charger.
 If your iPhone isn't charging or is charging slowly and your iPhone has a thick case, metal case, or battery case, try removing the case.
 If your iPhone vibrates—when it gets a notification, for example—your iPhone might shift position. This can cause the charging mat to stop providing power to your iPhone. If this happens often, consider turning off vibration , turning on Do Not Disturb , or using a case to prevent movement.
 Depending on the charging mat you have, you might hear faint noises while your iPhone charges.
 Your iPhone might get slightly warmer while it charges. To extend the lifespan of your battery, if the battery gets too warm, software might limit charging above 80 percent. Your iPhone will charge again when the temperature drops. Try moving your iPhone and charger to a cooler location.
 Your iPhone won't charge wirelessly when connected to USB. If your iPhone is connected to your computer with USB, or if it's connected to a USB power adapter, your iPhone will charge using the USB connection.
 With iPhone 15 models, if you're in the European Union or in a country or region that's part of the European Free Trade Association, the first time that you use a wireless charger, you'll get a notification. Mandated by the EU, the notification says that wireless charging might use more power than wired charging.
 Apple’s MagSafe wireless charging provides optimal magnetic alignment for faster, more efficient charging. MagSafe wireless charging includes technologies that reduce energy waste when compared to other wireless charging methods. Learn about charging with the MagSafe Charger and MagSafe Duo Charger .

Situation:
 
JLR Engineering investigations have found that iPhone 15 and iPhone 16 devices may intermittently stop charging or fail to charge when
placed on the vehicle wireless charging pad.
 
Symptoms may include:
• Charging starts, then disconnects.
• The message 'Phone not charging' displayed on the device screen.

Cause:
 
The design of the iPhone 15 / 16 range, particularly the Pro variants with a titanium frame, can falsely trigger the vehicle’s Foreign Object
Detection algorithm.
 
Wireless chargers use magnetic field attenuation thresholds to distinguish valid devices from foreign metallic objects, such as keys. In
some cases, the magnetic signature of these devices can be interpreted as a foreign object, causing charging to be suspended as a
safety precaution.

APPLICABLE MODEL(S)/VINS 
2023-2024 CX-50 (with Wireless Charger (Qi)) with VINS lower than 7MMVA******244893 (produced before July 24, 
2024)  
 
DESCRIPTION
Some customers may experience that despite placing the MagSafe®-equipped iPhone® at the center of the wireless 
charger, charging stops after about ten seconds. MagSafe-equipped iPhones use magnets to align the charger and the 
device. When charging MagSafe-equipped iPhones with a non-MagSafe compatible charger, improper alignment can 
cause the magnetic field required for charging to be disrupted by the magnets, significantly reducing charging efficiency.
The wireless charger (Qi) installed in the CX-50 is not MagSafe compatible and has a relatively small charging tray. 
Therefore, for larger devices such as iPhone 13 Pro Max, there may be insufficient space for proper alignment, resulting 
in decreased charging efficiency. 
Customers having this concern should have their vehicle repaired using the following repair procedure.
 
 
REPAIR PROCEDURE
1. Verify the customer concern.
2. Ensure the mobile device meets the following criteria:
a. The mobile device supports wireless charging (Qi).
b. The case of the mobile device is removed.
c. There are no foreign objects attached to the back of the mobile device.
d.  The NFC function of the mobile device is turned off.
e. The mobile device is not excessively hot.
f. The battery level of the mobile device is below 80%.
g. The charging side of the mobile device is facing the wireless charger.
h. The mobile device is not placed significantly off-center from the charging area.
3. Ensure the vehicle meets the following criteria:
a. The engine is running.
b. The hood, liftgate, and doors are fully closed.
c. The wireless charger (Qi) is turned on. 
NOTE: If the indicator is off, press and hold the ON/OFF button for more than 3 seconds to turn it on.
d. The wireless charger (Qi) is not overheated.
e. The location is not near strong radio waves or noise sources such as TV towers, power plants, or airports.

Safely fix iPhone or iPad charging on hold issue 
 Learn what to do if iPhone or iPad charging is on hold, and an alert pops up informing you that charging will resume when the device “returns to normal temperature.” 
 iOS’s built-in safety measures automatically pause charging when the battery’s internal temperature significantly exceeds the recommended operating temperature. You’re notified about this via a “Charging On Hold” notification on the Lock Screen.
 Here are some reasons   why your iPhone or iPad gets abnormally hot :
 It’s hot outside or you’ve left your iPhone plugged inside your car on a particularly hot summer day with the windows closed.
 You’ve been playing an intensive game for a long time, causing the processor to heat up.
 A thick case may cause your iPhone to overheat.
 You’ve unknowingly covered your iPhone charging on a bed or sofa with sheets or blankets, creating a hot air chamber that traps the heat.
 Wireless charging can heat up both the charger and your iPhone significantly.
 Massive fast chargers and no-name ones can cause your iPhone to get too hot.
 Any of these scenarios can create excessive heat, which could damage the device. To stop that from happening, iOS suspends charging until your iPhone cools down, rendering the device unusable until the temperature is within safety margins again.
 How to fix the “Charging On Hold” issue on iPhone and iPad
 The only solution for iPhone charging on hold is waiting until the internal temperature drops. Follow these tips to accelerate the cooling process.
 Unplug your iPhone. With no current, your iPhone may cool down faster.
 Turn off your iPhone and leave it unattended for at least 5 to 10 minutes.
 Remove the case to help the device dissipate heat better.
 If you have a fan or an air-conditioned room, put your iPhone in front of the airflow or relocate it to the air-conditioned room to help stabilize the internal temperature faster.
 When your iPhone reaches its safe operating temperature again, turn it on and plug it into power when it starts up. If you no longer see a “Charging on Hold” message, you’re good to go. Be sure to place your iPhone on a hard surface when charging instead of a mattress or cushion to avoid overheating and minimize fire hazard. If possible, charge over the wire instead of wirelessly.
 Note: Does your iPad case cover the entire backside? Whenever I use mine , I typically get the Charging On Hold alert, especially during the summer. Removing the case and laying my iPad on the table or using a stand which doesn’t cover the entire back  fixes this.
 Other solutions
 Consider these troubleshooting solutions if you get the ‘Charging On Hold’ alert even when you think your iPhone isn’t abnormally hot:
 1) Update to the latest version of iOS by going to Settings > General > Software Update and choosing  Download and Install or Install Now .
 Sometimes a software bug is the culprit. For example, iOS 17.0.3 contains a fix for the issue that caused the iPhone 15 Pros to overheat. If your iPhone keeps getting extra warm for no apparent reason, make sure to update to the latest iOS version.
 2) Reset all iPhone or iPad settings .
 3) If the device is running the latest iOS software and you’ve reset all settings, but the Charging On Hold alert hasn’t disappeared, you can erase your iPhone and set it up again. This is a nuclear option, so be sure to back up everything .

 Your iPhone gets warm when charging because pushing electricity into a lithium-ion battery is a chemical process that naturally produces heat, and fast charging, wireless pads, and using the phone at the same time all add to it. A little warmth is normal; a phone that feels genuinely hot or throws an overheating warning is telling you something needs to change.
 Quick answer: Mild warmth while charging is completely normal, especially during fast charging or the first 20 minutes on a 40W USB-C adapter. It becomes a problem when the phone is too hot to hold comfortably, charges painfully slowly, or shows a temperature warning. Fixes: take the case off, stop using the phone while it charges, move it out of the sun, and switch to a quality Apple-certified cable and adapter. Apple designs iPhone for ambient temperatures between 32°F and 95°F (0°C to 35°C).
 If you own an iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, or iPhone Air running iOS 26, you are also charging faster than older iPhones ever did, and faster charging means more heat. Below is a plain-English breakdown of every real cause, which ones are harmless, and exactly what to do about the ones that are not.
 Why charging produces heat in the first place
 Every rechargeable battery loses a small amount of energy as heat while it charges. Inside your iPhone, a charging chip converts and regulates the incoming power, and that conversion is never 100 percent efficient. The leftover energy becomes warmth. This is basic physics, not a defect, and it is why even a brand-new iPhone charging on the official cable gets slightly warm around the middle and lower back of the phone.
 Heat is highest at the start of a charge, when the battery is low and accepting power quickly, and it tapers off as the battery fills. That is why your phone often feels warmest in the first 20 to 30 minutes and cools down as it approaches 100 percent.
 Fast charging and USB-C Power Delivery
 The iPhone 17 lineup charges at up to 40W over USB-C using the Power Delivery (PD) standard, enough to reach about 50 percent in roughly 20 minutes with a 40W or higher adapter. Moving that much power quickly generates real heat as a trade-off for speed. This is expected and safe within limits, and iOS actively manages the temperature by throttling the charge speed if the phone gets too warm.
 Apple even builds a feature called thermally limited charging into iOS: when the phone senses it is running hot, it deliberately slows or pauses charging to protect the battery. So a warm phone that is charging a little slower than usual is often the system working exactly as designed, not failing.
 Wireless and MagSafe charging inefficiency
 Wireless charging is inherently less efficient than a cable. Energy is transferred across a small air gap between two coils, and whatever does not make it into the battery is released as heat. That is why an iPhone on a MagSafe or Qi2 pad frequently feels warmer than the same phone on a USB-C cable, even though MagSafe and Qi2 top out at 25W on the iPhone 17 versus 40W wired.
 Poor alignment makes it worse. If the phone is not centered on the coil, the charger works harder and generates more heat while delivering less power. A thick or metal-containing case can also interfere. If your phone runs hot on a wireless pad, reseat it until it snaps into place, or use a genuine MagSafe charger that aligns magnetically.
 Recommended for you:
 How-To Guides · Jul 11, 2026 How to Get Water Out of iPhone Speaker (2026) 
 Using the phone while it charges
 This is the single most common reason an iPhone gets uncomfortably hot on the charger. Charging generates heat, and so does the processor. Stack a demanding task on top of a charge and the two heat sources combine. Gaming, video streaming, GPS navigation, video calls, and camera use are the usual culprits. Set the phone down while it charges and it will run noticeably cooler.
 Heavy background tasks and processing
 Sometimes the phone is hot even though you are not touching it, because it is busy in the background. iCloud Photos syncing thousands of images, an app updating, a large download, or indexing after an update all push the processor while charging. A recent iOS 26 update, for example, re-optimizes the photo library and search index in the background, which can keep the phone warm for a while after you install it.
 Restoring, updating, or setting up a new iPhone
 The first hour or two with a new iPhone, or right after a major restore from backup, is a well-known warm period. The phone is downloading apps, syncing accounts, redownloading photos and messages, and charging at the same time. This can make a new iPhone 17 feel hot straight out of the box. It is normal and temporary. Let it finish, ideally with the case off, and the temperature returns to normal once setup completes.
 Direct sun, hot cars, and the environment
 Ambient heat matters enormously. Apple designs iPhone to operate in temperatures between 32°F and 95°F (0°C to 35°C). Charging in a car parked in the sun, on a windowsill, or on a dashboard mount stacks environmental heat on top of charging heat and can quickly trigger a temperature warning. Never leave a charging iPhone in a hot car. If you charge in a car mount that also runs navigation, keep it out of direct sunlight and in the airflow of an AC vent.
 A bad cable, adapter, or worn port
 Cheap, uncertified, or damaged cables and adapters are a real cause of excess heat. A frayed cable, a counterfeit charger, or a knockoff power bank can deliver unstable power that makes the charging circuit work harder and run hotter, and in rare cases poses a safety risk. Because the iPhone 17 ships with a cable but no wall adapter, a lot of people buy a random third-party brick. Use an Apple-certified (MFi) cable and a reputable USB-C PD adapter. Also check the port for lint or debris, which traps heat and blocks a clean connection.
 A case that traps heat
 Thick, insulating cases, especially rugged or battery cases, hold heat against the phone with nowhere to escape. This is most noticeable during fast or wireless charging. If your iPhone consistently runs hot on the charger, take the case off while it charges. It is the easiest fix on this list and often the most effective.
 Battery health and aging
 As a battery ages, its internal resistance rises and it becomes less efficient, which means more of the charging energy turns into heat. An iPhone that is two or three years old and has been through hundreds of charge cycles will naturally run a bit warmer and charge a bit slower than it did when new. Check Settings, Battery, Battery Health & Charging. If Maximum Capacity has dropped well below 80 percent, a battery replacement will restore both cooler charging and longer runtime.
 Software bugs and rogue apps
 Occasionally the cause is software. A buggy app stuck in a loop, a bad background process, or a glitch shortly after an iOS update can keep the processor working overtime and the phone hot. Check Settings, Battery to see if one app is using a disproportionate amount of power. Force-quitting it, updating it, or restarting the phone usually clears it. If a new iOS 26 point update introduced the problem, installing the next patch often fixes it.
 How to fix an iPhone that gets hot when charging
 Take the case off. Remove any case while charging, especially during fast or wireless charging, so heat can dissipate.
 Stop using the phone. Put it down and avoid gaming, streaming, navigation, or camera use while it charges.
 Move it somewhere cool. Get it out of direct sun, off hot surfaces, and out of parked cars. Aim for room temperature.
 Check your cable and adapter. Use an Apple-certified cable and a reputable USB-C PD adapter. Retire any frayed cable or no-name brick.
 Clean the charging port. Gently remove lint or debris with a wooden or plastic toothpick, never metal.
 Reseat wireless chargers. Center the phone on the pad or use MagSafe so it aligns correctly and charges efficiently.
 Switch to a cable if wireless runs hot. A USB-C cable is more efficient and cooler than a wireless pad.
 Restart the phone. A quick restart clears a stuck app or background process that is generating heat.
 Check Battery settings. Look for a rogue app under Battery, and review Battery Health & Charging for a worn battery.
 Update iOS and your apps. Install the latest iOS 26 update and app updates to clear known bugs.
 Let new-phone setup finish. If you just set up or restored the phone, let it complete before judging the temperature.
 Normal versus concerning: a quick reference
 Cause Is it normal? What to do 
 Mild warmth during fast charging Yes Nothing; it cools as the battery fills 
 Warm on a MagSafe or Qi2 pad Yes Center the phone; switch to cable if excessive 
 Hot while gaming or navigating on charge Somewhat Put the phone down while charging 
 Warm during setup or restore Yes Let it finish; remove the case 
 Hot in the sun or a hot car No Move it somewhere cool immediately 
 Very hot with a cheap or damaged cable No Replace with certified gear now 
 Hot with a temperature warning No Unplug, power off, let it cool 
 Runs hot and charges slowly as it ages Partly Check battery health; replace if worn 
 Recommended for you:
 Gaming · Jul 10, 2026 How to Fix PS5 Controller Stick Drift (2026): 7 Working Methods 
 When to worry
 Warmth you can comfortably hold is fine. Start paying attention when the phone becomes genuinely hot to the touch, when you see a “Charging On Hold” notification (which means the phone is temporarily too hot or too cold to charge), or when the full-screen temperature warning appears and the display dims. At that point iOS has paused charging and possibly disabled the camera and flash to cool down. An iPhone showing the temperature warning may still be able to make emergency calls.
 If you get a warning, unplug the phone, power it off, take the case off, and move it out of any heat source. Do not put it in a refrigerator or freezer; rapid cooling causes condensation that can damage the electronics. Just let it return to room temperature on its own. Seek help if the phone overheats repeatedly with no obvious cause, becomes hot enough to be uncomfortable to hold, swells or bulges anywhere, or emits any smell. A swollen battery is a safety issue and should be handled by Apple or an authorized service provider, not used or charged.
 For a deeper look at charging your iPhone quickly and safely, see our guide to iPhone 17 Pro charging, charger types, and speeds , and if heat and battery life are pushing you toward a new phone, compare the field in which iPhone has the best battery life .
 The bottom line
 An iPhone getting warm while charging is normal, and on the fast-charging iPhone 17 lineup it is more noticeable than ever. The heat you should ignore is mild, temporary, and worst in the first 20 minutes of a charge. The heat you should act on is the kind that makes the phone hard to hold, slows charging to a crawl, or triggers a warning. In almost every case the fix is simple: take the case off, stop using the phone while it charges, keep it out of the sun and hot cars, and use a good certified cable and adapter. Do that, keep an eye on your battery health, and your iPhone will charge cool, safe, and fast.

iPhone Won’t Charge After the iOS 27 Update? Apple Documents Heat as a Cause, Not a Fault
iPhone Won’t Charge After the iOS 27 Update? Apple Documents Heat as a Cause, Not a Fault
Mike Peterson

 3 minute read
Sep 12th, 2026 5:27 PM EEST | News
Image: Apple

A phone that will not charge, or charges slower than expected, right after a major update is a specific enough scare that Apple has a dedicated support page for it. The explanation is heat, and Apple treats it as expected behavior rather than damage.

A major software update is one of the causes Apple names for a device running warm enough to pause charging. Image: Apple

Apple’s temperature support article, 118431, states plainly: “Charging, including wireless charging, slows or stops” when a device is too warm. The same page lists “complete a software update, particularly to a major release” among the documented causes of that warmth, and iOS 27, arriving Monday, September 14, qualifies as exactly that.

Key facts on charging and heat after an update
Detail	What Apple documents
Effect of warmth on charging	“Charging, including wireless charging, slows or stops”
A documented cause of warmth	“Complete a software update, particularly to a major release”
A second documented cause of warmth	“Wirelessly charge your device”, listed separately
Dedicated charging-heat article	Support article 104949, “your iPhone or iPad is temporarily too hot or too cold to charge”
Apple’s fix	Turn the device off, move it to a cooler environment away from direct sunlight, let it cool
Duration of the pause	Not published
iOS 27 is a major release, the category of update Apple lists among documented causes of device warmth. Image: Apple
The symptom Apple explains, once you find the page

The instinct when a phone stops charging is to suspect a cable, an adapter, or damage to the port. Apple’s own documentation offers a more mundane explanation first: the device is warm, charging has paused as a protection, and it will resume once the temperature drops. That explanation lives on the general temperature page, 118431, and a second, dedicated article, 104949, exists specifically for this symptom.

118431 also states the range a device is designed to operate within: 0º to 35ºC (32º to 95ºF). A device that strays outside that range, for whatever combination of reasons, is the condition both articles describe, and neither treats it as evidence of a hardware problem on its own.

Apple's charging figures for iPhone 18 Pro assume a device within its documented operating temperature range. Image: Apple
Why an update and a wireless charger can stack

Apple’s list of warmth causes includes completing a major update and wirelessly charging a device as two separate entries. Plugging an iPhone in to charge wirelessly while it finishes installing iOS 27, or immediately after, combines two documented sources of heat rather than one, which makes a charging pause more likely to appear right at that moment, not less explicable.

Documented cause of warmth	Relevant to update day
Complete a software update, particularly a major release	Directly describes iOS 27 on September 14
Wirelessly charge your device	Common if a device is placed on a charger during or after the update
Restore from a backup	Applies to anyone setting up a device around the same update
What Apple says to do

The instructions are the same regardless of which combination of causes applies: turn the device off, move it somewhere cooler and out of direct sunlight, and let it cool down before charging again. Apple’s page also notes that a device showing the temperature warning screen might still be able to make emergency calls, which is worth knowing before assuming the device has failed outright.

Nothing in either article distinguishes a fix for a wired charge from a fix for a wireless one. The remedy Apple publishes addresses the temperature, not the cable, which is consistent with treating the cause as heat rather than a connection or accessory fault.

What Apple has not said

Apple’s documentation resolves the “why” without resolving the “how long” or the specifics of update day:

No duration is published for how long a charging pause caused by warmth typically lasts.
No statement distinguishes a pause caused by finishing an update from one caused by wireless charging alone.
Neither 118431 nor 104949 has been revised to mention iOS 27 specifically.
No wired-versus-wireless recommendation is published for a device that is warm from an update.

iOS 27 becomes available Monday, September 14. A device that pauses charging that day or in the days after, according to Apple’s own pages, is behaving as documented rather than failing.  Quick Answer: Your iPhone gets very hot when charging because of a faulty charger, running apps while plugged in, background processes, a bad iOS update, or a degraded battery . 
Remove your case, unplug for 10–15 minutes, and restart. If the heat keeps returning, work through the nine fixes below to prevent iPhone overheating in order.
 Your iPhone just got scorching hot on the charger.
 Not warm — hot .
 Hot enough to make you yank the cable out and wonder if something is seriously wrong.
 You’re not alone, and no, your phone is not about to explode.
 Main Topics 
 Why Does Your iPhone Get So Hot When Charging? How to Fix Your iPhone Getting Hot When Charging: 9 Steps Real-World Case Study What If None of These Fixes Work? Frequently Asked Questions 
 But you do need to fix this today, because persistent overheating quietly destroys your battery’s long-term health.
 We’ve seen this issue spike with the iOS 26 rollout in late 2025, particularly on iPhone 14 overheating issues and iPhone 15 and 16 models using third-party USB-C accessories.
 Here’s everything you need to know – and exactly what to do about it.
 Why iPhone Overheating?
 An iPhone getting very hot when charging is usually fixable at home – start with the charger and case .
 Non-certified cables are the #1 overlooked cause of charging heat in 2026, especially on iPhone 15/16/17 USB-C models.
 iOS 26.5 patches known background processing bugs that caused overheating on iOS 26.0–26.2.
 Battery health below 80% generates excess heat — a battery replacement often solves chronic heat problems permanently.
 Never cool an overheating iPhone in a fridge — gradual cooling at room temperature is the only safe method.
 Enable Optimized Battery Charging to reduce long-term heat buildup and preserve battery lifespan.
 If you see a swollen battery or a temperature warning screen, seek professional repair immediately.
 Why Does Your iPhone Get So Hot When Charging?
 Think of your iPhone’s processor like a car engine. Charging already generates heat — add a navigation app running in the background and you’re essentially flooring the gas while parked. The engine overheats.

 Your iPhone is designed to operate between 32°F and 95°F (0°C–35°C) . Anything beyond that triggers Apple’s built-in thermal throttling, and you’ll see performance slow to a crawl. Here are the most common culprits:
 Non-certified charger or cable – Cheap third-party cables deliver inconsistent voltage. This forces your battery to work harder, and it gets very hot fast. – READ MORE 
 Running apps while charging – Games, GPS navigation, or FaceTime while plugged in stacks heat from both charging and processing.
 Background processes – iCloud sync, iOS updates installing, or Spotlight reindexing can run silently and spike your CPU.
 Phone case trapping heat – Thick silicone or wallet cases block heat dissipation entirely.
 Environmental heat – Charging on a bed, in direct sunlight, or inside a hot car dramatically reduces your phone’s ability to cool itself.
 Degraded battery – If your battery health is below 80%, it generates more heat during every charge cycle. Check this at Settings → Battery → Battery Health & Charging .
 iOS software bug – The iOS 26.0 and 26.1 releases introduced background indexing bugs that caused iPhone constantly overheating reports across Reddit and Apple’s support forums. iOS 26.5 patches this.
 How to Fix Your iPhone Getting Hot When Charging: 9 Steps
 Step 1: Unplug and Cool Down Immediately 
 When your iPhone suddenly gets hot , stop charging right away.
 Unplug the charger from your iPhone.
 Remove your protective case completely.
 Set the iPhone on a hard, flat surface – not a bed or couch.
 Move it to a cool, shaded, well-ventilated area.
 Wait 10–15 minutes . Do not place it in a fridge or freezer — rapid temperature changes damage the battery.
 When we tested this on our iPhone 17 Pro running iOS 26.5 , we found that simply removing the case and setting the phone on a desk dropped the surface temperature by about 8°F in under five minutes.
 Step 2: Switch to an Apple-Certified Charger 
 This is the single most overlooked cause of iPhone overheating and not charging properly.
 A non-MFi certified cable doesn’t just charge slowly — it can push irregular voltage that forces your battery to generate excess heat.
 Use only Apple’s official cable or an MFi-certified (Made for iPhone) alternative.
 For iPhone 15, 16, and 17: use a USB-C cable rated for 27W or higher.
 Plug into a wall outlet , not a laptop USB port or power strip with a weak adapter.
 Apple’s 20W USB-C Power Adapter is the minimum recommended charger for all current models.
 Step 3: Remove Your Case During Charging 
 A thick case is basically a heat blanket. If your iPhone gets warm when charging even with a certified cable, try charging without the case for a full cycle and compare temperatures.
 Step 4: Force Restart Your iPhone 
 A force restart clears temporary software processes that can cause iPhone heating up while using — even when the screen looks idle.
 For iPhone 8, SE (2nd/3rd gen), iPhone X through iPhone 17: 
 Press and quickly release the Volume Up button.
 Press and quickly release the Volume Down button.
 Press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears. Release.
 For iPhone 7 / 7 Plus: 
 Press and hold Volume Down + Side until the Apple logo appears.
 Related:  How to Restart iPhone (iOS 26 Updated Guide) 
 Step 5: Update to the Latest iOS Version 
 Apple released iOS 26.5 in May 2026 specifically to address background processing bugs that caused iPhone overheating not working normally after charging. If you’re on iOS 26.0–26.2, this update is essential.
 Go to Settings → General → Software Update and install any available update. Do this on Wi-Fi with the phone plugged in — but monitor the temperature. If it overheats during the update, unplug, let it cool, and resume on battery.
 Step 6: Disable Background App Refresh and Location Services 
 Background processes are a silent heat generator. Here’s how to tame them:
 Go to Settings → General → Background App Refresh . Set it to Off or Wi-Fi Only .
 Go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services . Set non-essential apps to Never or While Using .
 Go to Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud and turn off syncing for apps you don’t urgently need updated.
 Pro Tip: Check Battery Health Before Anything Else
 If your iPhone 14 overheating issues or iPhone 15/16 heat problems persist no matter what you try, the real culprit may be your battery. Go to Settings → Battery → Battery Health & Charging . If Maximum Capacity reads below 80% , the battery is degraded and generates significantly more heat during every charge. Apple’s battery replacement runs $89–$99 in 2026 — often the single best fix for chronic heat problems on older devices.
 Step 7: Enable Optimized Battery Charging 
 This feature prevents your iPhone from staying at 100% for extended periods — which generates continuous heat and degrades the battery faster.
 Go to Settings → Battery → Battery Health & Charging → Optimized Battery Charging and toggle it On . For a deeper breakdown of how this works, read our guide on what Optimized Battery Charging actually does .
 Step 8: Reset All Settings (No Data Loss) 
 If your iPhone is constantly overheating after charging and the fixes above haven’t worked, a settings conflict from a bad iOS update or restored backup may be the cause.
 Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Reset → Reset All Settings . This resets Wi-Fi passwords, privacy settings, and display preferences — but deletes no photos or apps. After the reset, test charging from scratch before restoring any settings.
 Step 9: Check for Hardware Damage or Battery Swelling 
 If your iPhone feels noticeably thicker near the bottom or the screen appears slightly lifted at one corner, stop charging immediately. This can indicate a swollen battery , which is a safety issue requiring immediate service.
 Contact Apple Support at apple.com/support or visit an Apple Authorized Service Provider. Do not attempt to open the device yourself.
 Learn why your iPhone gets dangerously hot while charging and discover 9 proven fixes that actually work in 2026. Real-World Case Study
 Sarah, 29, from Chicago reached out after her iPhone 15 Pro got too hot to hold every night while charging.
 She’d been using a USB-C cable she bought at an airport kiosk. She switched to the Apple cable that came with her phone and plugged directly into her wall adapter instead of a multi-port hub on her desk.
 The overheating stopped completely that same night.
 Her battery health was at 91% — still healthy. The culprit was a $9 cable delivering inconsistent power, causing her battery to fight for every watt.
 What If None of These Fixes Work?
 If your iPhone is still getting dangerously hot after every fix above, here’s the escalation path:
 Does it only overheat while charging? → Suspect charger hardware or charging port damage.
 Does it overheat even on battery? → Suspect a runaway app or iOS bug. Check Settings → Battery for which app is using the most energy.
 Does it show a temperature warning screen? → Apple has completely locked the device for safety. Let it cool for 30+ minutes before use.
 Is the phone also not turning on? → See our guide on what to do when iPhone won’t turn on for recovery mode steps.
 Still no resolution? → Book an appointment with an Apple Authorized Service Provider. They can run diagnostics to check the battery, charging circuit, and thermal management system.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Q1: Is it normal for an iPhone to get warm while charging? Yes — slight warmth is completely normal, especially during fast charging or if you’re using the phone simultaneously. “Warm” is fine. “Hot enough to be uncomfortable to hold” is not, and indicates an issue that needs fixing.
 Q2: Can charging overnight damage my iPhone battery? With Optimized Battery Charging enabled, it’s generally safe. The feature holds charge at 80% and only completes to 100% just before you typically wake up. Without it, staying at 100% for hours generates heat that accelerates battery aging. Learn more in our Optimized Battery Charging guide .
 Q3: Why does my iPhone 14 keep overheating specifically? iPhone 14 overheating issues spiked after the iOS 16.x and iOS 17.x update cycles due to background indexing bugs. The same pattern repeated with iOS 26.0. Updating to the latest iOS version and resetting all settings resolves the majority of these cases.
 Q4: Does does iPhone heat while charging with MagSafe too? Yes — MagSafe generates slightly more heat than wired charging due to wireless energy conversion losses. If your iPhone gets very hot on MagSafe, make sure it’s not in a case that blocks airflow, and avoid using the phone heavily while on the charger.
 Q5: My iPhone is overheating and not charging at the same time — what do I do? First, unplug and cool down for 15 minutes. Then force restart (Step 4 above). Try a different certified cable and adapter. If it’s still not charging after cooling down and restarting, read our complete guide on iPhone not charging fixes for the full diagnostic path.
